If you’re new to the podcast, welcome! Here’s an overview of the format and style, to give you an idea of what to expect, so you can decide whether to join me. In our weekly program, we share stories from the world of quantum theory, astrophysics, neuroscience and technology, in an accessible way that makes it easy to understand. We also cover the latest research, and examine ideas and theories from the past that may or may not hold true today. In each episode, we present scientific research, and draw parallels with our personal lives and personal experiences.
In addition to podcast episodes, we also have a Facebook group. In the Facebook group, we answer questions from members, and share more about the theories and concepts we discuss on the podcast. We also share a variety of resources, including articles, videos and links. We’ve hosted several virtual meetups and online courses. All this is done so that the science can be understood and appreciated by the masses.
The podcast is not intended to replace scientific education, but is intended to complement it and provide a platform for interesting and thought-provoking discussions. If you’re looking for science podcasts that are more serious and detailed, there are a lot of options. The science podcasts listed below are ones I’ve heard that I thought were worthwhile, and that I recommend to anyone interested in science. If you’re looking for a podcast where topics are explored in more detail, or where the science is presented in a more straightforward way, then there are other podcasts available that are more suitable.</s>

The seventh ecstasy is what the shorthand makes it sound like, the place where the shorthand is broken, the place where there is no projection, where there is a stillness. The seventh ecstasy is a place where the words are no more.</s>

Its subject is unruly, fragmented, and unsettlingly real — a place that only exists on the surface of the earth — and it seems to be in the process of disappearing, as it is being slowly eroded.

This recording is not the record of the death that it is here represented. It is the record of its death, not by death, as a stillness of the heart, a stoppage in the brain. The recording of the loss in this book has been suspended between this present moment and the moment of its transposition in the surface of the book. It has been suspended by the absence of words, as an infinite number of words has been suspended for the moment, until one of these words takes up the place where the recording was suspended.</s>
